scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: After rain, a perfect arc of colours appears in the sky. Where do all those colours come from?

scenes.name: white
scenes.text: Sunlight looks white, but it's actually a mix of all colours, from red to violet.

scenes.name: bend
scenes.text: When light enters a raindrop, it slows down and bends. This is called refraction.

scenes.name: split
scenes.text: Each colour bends by a slightly different amount, so the white light fans out into a spectrum.

scenes.name: reflect
scenes.text: Inside the drop, light reflects off the back, and comes out toward you, at about forty two degrees.

scenes.name: position
scenes.text: That's why you only see a rainbow with the sun behind you. Millions of drops each send you one colour.

scenes.name: double
scenes.text: A second bounce inside drops makes a fainter double rainbow, with its colours in reverse order.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Bend, split, bounce. Every drop a tiny prism. Follow for more on how things really work.
